text: Veterinary medicine residues are small amounts of medicine left in meat, eggs, or milk after treatment; eating these products soon after treatment means absorbing small doses of the medicine. Risks include allergic reactions (e.g. some people are allergic to Penicillin, and even trace amounts can trigger a reaction), antibiotic resistance (regularly eating products with Tetracycline traces has been linked to E. coli developing Tetracycline resistance in humans), and toxicity (Chloramphenicol traces can cause fatal anemia in humans). Prevention: manufacturers state a withdrawal period on the label — the waiting time after treatment before the animal's meat, eggs, or milk can be safely eaten — and good general practice is to use medicine only when actually necessary (better management often solves most health problems), and when medicine is needed, to use a good-quality product at the correct dosage for the correct duration.
